editorial:
Ever felt like your math homework was literally trying to kill you? You will totally relate to the main character here, a struggling student who is so done with failing geometry that he decides to take a huge risk. Instead of studying, he uses an old book to summon a demon to do the work for him. It starts off as a funny idea, but things get weird fast. The movie has a great mix of spooky monster vibes and teen comedy that makes it feel like a wild ride from start to finish. You get to see a young Guillermo del Toro playing with creepy visuals while keeping the story light and silly.

What really works is how the tension builds up as the demon starts asking for things in return. The acting is spot on, and the practical effects look great for a movie from the eighties. Some parts move a bit slow in the middle, but the ending makes up for it. If you love weird creature features, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the final act, the demon reveals that it does not want money or souls, but instead wants to take over the boy's physical body to experience the human world. The boy has to use the very geometry rules he hated to trick the demon back into its realm. He draws a perfect circle around the creature, trapping it forever. He ends up passing his class, but he is way too scared to ever open a math book again.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s horror and dark humor.
